title: The boycott
hookLine: Quraysh boycott the Prophet's clan, who live three years in a valley near starvation

cards: No sword, this time. No rock on anyone's chest. Just a sheet of writing.

Back in Mecca, Ibn Ishaq says, the leaders of Quraysh saw the Muslims safe in Abyssinia, Hamzah and Umar on the Prophet's side, and the message spreading among the clans. So they tried something slower.
They drew up a document, agreed to it together, and hung it inside the Ka'ba to make it binding. It was aimed at one family. Today: the boycott.

teach.b: The terms, as Ibn Ishaq gives them, were simple. No one would marry into the clans of Hashim and al-Muttalib, or give them anyone in marriage. No one would sell to them, or buy from them.
Cut off the family, and the man at its center would be handed over or starve with them. The clan didn't hand him over.
Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib went with Abu Talib into his valley on the edge of Mecca, the shi'b, and Ibn Ishaq says they went together, believers and unbelievers alike.
Abu Lahab, he says, left his clan and sided with Quraysh.

So the boycott shut in people who did not share the Prophet's faith, only his blood. And they went hungry. Ibn Ishaq says they were worn down, and almost nothing reached them except what was smuggled in.

He tells of Hakim ibn Hizam with a servant carrying wheat for his aunt Khadijah, until Abu Jahl caught him and tried to stop it, and another Meccan stepped in and let the food pass. How long did it last?
Ibn Ishaq says two or three years; today's line rounds it to three. A document hung inside the Ka'ba, used to starve a family. The family's answer was to stay together.

how: Muslims retell the boycott in sirah lessons as the time the Prophet's clan was confined to the valley of Abu Talib, and point to the clan's loyalty, believers and unbelievers together.

practice: Choose one thing you'll eat, drink or buy today that you could do without, a coffee, a snack, a second helping, and choose where it goes instead: a food bank, a neighbor, someone who's struggling.
Notice the small pull of wanting it anyway; in the valley, that pull lasted for years. If you pray, you can remember the hungry by name.

wordCard.voice: The boycott. Quraysh agree in writing to cut off the Prophet's clan, no marriage and no trade, and the clan holds together in the valley, hungry. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a mountain pass or narrow valley; the shi'b of Abu Talib, where the clan was confined.

carryVoice: Your line: three years hungry. They shared his blood, not all of them his faith, and they stayed. Day seven hundred forty-five, done.
